about.title: A library built to last
about.lead: Lumen begins with a simple conviction: great texts deserve a reading experience to match. We bring Spiritist works in the public domain together, care for their presentation and keep technology out of the way.
about.missionBody: To make Spiritist thought accessible, readable and searchable in four languages, while respecting every reader's autonomy. We do not sell certainties: we offer texts, context and tools for thinking.
about.preservationBody: Every complete edition receives metadata review, standardised cover treatment and public-domain verification. Source, original edition and licence are recorded on each work page and in our provenance document.
about.technologyTitle: Technology in the service of reading
about.technologyBody: Next.js with static rendering, in-browser EPUB and PDF readers, Pagefind search and local persistence with IndexedDB. No trackers, no sign-up and no cloud dependency for your shelf.
about.accessibilityBody: Contrast, visible focus, keyboard navigation, alternative text and respect for reduced-motion preferences. Read-aloud tools and typographic adjustments remain under your control.
about.rightsBody: The works by Allan Kardec, Camille Flammarion and Arthur Conan Doyle included here are in the public domain. We use original French and English editions so that no modern translation is reused. Covers, descriptions and introductory texts are Lumen’s own editorial work.
about.rightsAuthorsBody: Chico Xavier, Divaldo Pereira Franco and Yvonne do Amaral Pereira remain protected by copyright. Lumen provides only biographical profiles and links to their official publishers; no protected text is hosted in this project.
about.privacyBody: We use no advertising trackers. Favourites, reading progress and the newsletter sign-up stay in your browser through IndexedDB. The only exception is the contact form, which sends what you type to the project's local storage. You can erase everything by clearing this site's data.
about.sampleBody: The editions are complete and were obtained from public collections: Wikisource, Internet Archive and Project Gutenberg. Original French and English sources are preserved; Portuguese, Spanish and English descriptions describe the works but do not replace licensed translations.
about.faq1Question: Do I need an account to read?
about.faq1Answer: No. All reading is open. Favourites and progress stay in your browser and are not sent to servers.
about.faq2Answer: Yes. Once a work is open, the file can be downloaded as EPUB or PDF. Progress and your shelf remain local.
about.faq3Answer: The Pagefind index is generated at build time in four languages. Search runs in the browser and never sends your queries away.
about.faq4Question: Can I contribute to the collection?
about.faq4Answer: The project is designed to receive new public-domain editions. Curation prioritises accurate metadata, accessibility and editorial clarity.
